title: Advertising
summary: Advertising is the activity of presenting a sponsored message about a product, service or idea to prospective customers to make them aware of it and induce them to buy. The American Marketing Association defines it as 'any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods and services by an identified sponsor'. The firm that pays is the sponsor or advertiser; the message is the advertisement; the newspaper, TV or hoarding that carries it is the medium. DAGMAR (Defining Advertising Goals for Measured Advertising Results) is a method of setting and measuring advertising goals.

(1) Non-personal — no face-to-face contact; addressed to people in general (mass communication). (2) Paid form of communication — the sponsor pays for space or time. (3) Promotion of a product, service or idea. (4) Identified sponsor — the advertiser's name is always disclosed. (5) Communicated through media. (6) It aims to inform and persuade. Advertising is a powerful communication force and an important part of the promotion mix (with personal selling, sales promotion and publicity). It is not flexible — once fixed, the message cannot be changed to suit each customer.

(1) Educating customers about products and their uses (Tata Namak with iodine). (2) Creating demand for new products (gel pens). (3) Retaining existing customers and maintaining demand by reminding them (Nirma). (4) Increasing sales of existing as well as new products. (5) Assisting salesmen — customers already know the product's features. (6) Helping mass production and lowering costs; building the image of the firm; facing competition. For society it creates employment and supports newspapers and TV.

Print media — newspapers and periodicals (press advertising). Newspapers: wide circulation, low cost, can be repeated daily, flexible (changes at short notice), available in many languages for regional markets; but short life, read casually, useless for illiterates. Best for consumer goods for the general public, new launches, clearance sales and exchange offers; a local edition suits local businesses such as a coaching institute. Periodicals (weekly, monthly magazines — India Today, Femina, Reader's Digest): longer life than newspapers, selective readership (Femina for women's products such as sarees and herbal cosmetics), good printing; but costlier, smaller reach, less flexible.

Electronic media — radio, television, Internet. Radio: heard regularly, reaches illiterates and people in remote areas, can be heard while travelling or working; but no visual impact and easily forgotten. Television: most effective because it has audio-visual impact; products can be demonstrated; slogans and celebrities have lasting impact; wide choice of channels; reaches illiterates — but costly to make and telecast, and viewers switch channels in breaks. Internet: information from all over the world within a fraction of a second, available any time; but needs a computer or phone and skill, not for illiterates.

Other (outdoor) media — hoardings (large boards painted or electronically designed, visible day and night), posters (on walls and bridges), vehicular or transit displays (advertisements on buses and trains, which carry the message to many people), gift items, neon signs. The choice of medium depends on the nature of the product, the target customers, the funds available and the space and time available. For the blind, radio is the medium; for illiterates, radio, television and cinema.

vsa: State any two advantages of newspaper advertising.

(1) Wide circulation — one advertisement reaches a very large number of people quickly at low cost.
(2) Flexibility — it can be given or changed at short notice and repeated daily; regional and language editions reach the desired market.
Which medium of advertising would the blind prefer? Which media are useful for illiterate consumers?

The blind: radio, because it depends only on hearing.
Illiterates: radio, television and cinema, which do not require reading.
What is meant by advertising? State two of its features.

Advertising is any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods and services by an identified sponsor.
Features: (1) it is paid; (2) the sponsor is identified (also non-personal, carried through media).
State any two limitations of television advertising.

(1) It is very costly to prepare and telecast.
(2) With so many advertisements, viewers switch channels during commercial breaks, so the impact falls.
sa: State any three points on the importance of advertising.

(1) It educates customers about products and their uses.
(2) It creates demand for new products and maintains demand for existing ones.
(3) It increases sales and assists salesmen, and helps the firm face competition.
What is television advertising? Explain any two advantages.

Television advertising means showing advertisements on TV channels during breaks or in sponsored programmes.
(1) Audio-visual impact — products can be seen, heard and demonstrated, so it is the most effective medium.
(2) Lasting impact and wide reach — catchy slogans, music and celebrities are remembered; it reaches even illiterate viewers through regional channels.
Describe any three objectives of advertising.

(1) To educate customers about a product and its use.
(2) To create demand for a new product.
(3) To retain existing customers and increase sales; also to assist salesmen.
Which form of advertising connects customers to information from all over the world within a fraction of a second? State two advantages and two limitations.

Internet advertising.
Advantages: information from all over the world at the doorstep; can be seen at any time as required.
Limitations: needs a computer or smartphone with Internet; not suitable for illiterates or those who cannot use the Internet.
la: What is meant by advertising? Explain its features.

Advertising is any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods and services by an identified sponsor.
(1) Non-personal — there is no face-to-face contact; it is directed to the public in general.
(2) Paid form of communication — the advertiser pays for space or time in the media.
(3) Promotion of a product, service or idea — it informs people and induces them to buy.
(4) Identified sponsor — the name of the advertiser is always disclosed.
(5) Communicated through media — newspapers, TV, radio, Internet, hoardings.
A company launching a women's health magazine wants to promote herbal cosmetics and kitchen appliances. Which media should it use and why?

Its own women's magazine and other women's periodicals (like Femina) — selective readership of women, longer life, good colour printing.
Television — audio-visual demonstration of kitchen appliances during family serials and cookery shows.
Internet and social media — targeted advertising to women, available any time.
Newspapers (women's supplements) for wide reach at low cost.
The choice follows the target customers (women), the nature of the products (need demonstration) and the budget.

or: Describe any five points of importance of advertising.

(1) Educates customers about products and their uses.
(2) Creates demand for new products.
(3) Retains customers and maintains demand.
(4) Increases sales and helps mass production at lower cost.
(5) Assists salesmen and builds the goodwill of the firm; also creates employment and supports the media.

la: What is meant by advertising? Give two features and explain three objectives.

Advertising is a paid, non-personal presentation and promotion of goods, services or ideas by an identified sponsor.
Features: paid; identified sponsor.
Objectives: (1) to educate customers; (2) to create demand for new products; (3) to retain existing customers and increase sales.
Is advertising necessary for business? Discuss.

Yes. (1) Customers must know about a product before they can buy it — advertising informs them. (2) It creates demand for new products and keeps demand for old ones. (3) It increases sales, making large-scale production and lower costs possible. (4) It helps salesmen and builds the firm's image. (5) In a competitive market a firm that does not advertise loses customers to rivals.
What is advertising? Explain two objectives and the media of advertising.

Advertising is a paid, non-personal promotion of goods, services or ideas by an identified sponsor.
Objectives: create demand; educate customers (also retain customers, increase sales).
Media: print — newspapers, periodicals; electronic — radio, television, Internet; outdoor — hoardings, posters, vehicular displays.
